newsitem.title: USA: Ashland, Texaco no comment on Nigeria deal rumors.
newsitem.headline: Ashland, Texaco no comment on Nigeria deal rumors.

text.p: Texaco Inc on Friday declined to comment on rumors that it was talking to Ashland Inc about purchasing the latter's Nigerian upstream assets.
Ashland also declined comment, except to reiterate that talks on a sale of those assets were continuing with French oil major Total SA
"Until we've got something concrete it is inappropriate for us to comment," a Texaco spokesman said.

Ashland spokesman Stan Lampe said: "Ashland has met with the honorable oil minister of Nigeria, the talks were constructive. We are currently in discussions with Total, but these talks are confidential, and that's all we're saying."
Oil industry sources in Nigeria said it was widely rumoured that Texaco and Ashland executives in the U.S. discussed the possibility of a deal.

Ashland, as part of the company's restructuring announced last year, had in June of this year transferred its Nigerian interests to a private French company, Persenco Investments S.A. However, the Nigerian oil ministry revoked Ashland's operating license, saying the company had not been cleared to make the transfer.
Ashland's interest include crude oil equity share of about six offshore fields of about 17,000 barrels per day and an offshore floating terminal.
